title: List as the image of a finite set
statement: Let $l$ be a duplicate-free list in a type with decidable equality, let $S$ be a finite set, and let $g$ map the elements of $S$'s ambient type to the list's ambient type. Suppose $g$ is injective, every entry of $l$ is the image under $g$ of some element of $S$, and the length of $l$ equals the cardinality of $S$. Then the set of entries of $l$ is exactly the image of $S$ under $g$.
